texts.preamble: Sh. Ratan Jeet Singh Gulati vs State Through on 28 August, 2018 In The Court Of Ms.Poonam A.Bamba District & Sessions Judge New Delhi In the matters of : Fsat No. 47/16 1. Sh. Ratan Jeet Singh Gulati S/o Sh. Bal Raj Gulati R/o B377, Gali No. 4, Adarsh Nagar Delhi110009. (FBOCumNominee) M/s Future Consumer Enterprises Ltd. 2. M/s Future Consumer Enterprises Ltd.(Big Apple) Shop No. 5 and 6, Hudson Lane Kingsway Camp, Delhi110009. Through A.R. ..... Appellants Versus State Through Sh . D.V. Singh (Food Safety Officer) Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place, New Delhi 110001. ..... Respondent Appeal On Behalf Of The Appellant Against The Order Dated 18.04.2016 Of Ld. Adm, New Delhi. Fsat No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. Fso Date of filing of appeal Arguments concluded on Date of judgment J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: 1.0 Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the appeal against the order dated 18.04.2016 ("the impugned order" in short) passed by the Ld. Addl. District Magistrate (New Delhi) ("ADM" in short), directing the appellant to pay a penalty of Rs1,00,000/, under section 53 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short), within 7 days from the date of order. Sh. Ratan Jeet Singh Gulati vs State Through on 28 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164219645/ 1 2.0 Facts in brief which are not in dispute, are that : i) on 05.06.2015, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short), lifted the sample of "Noodles (Veg. Hakka)", from the possession of appellant (FBOcumNominee) of M/s Future Consumer Enterprises Ltd., Shop No. 5&6, Hudson Lane, Kingsway Camp, Delhi110 009, where the said food article was found stored for sale for human consumption. One counterpart of the sample under sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst; FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO ii) The Food Analyst vide his report dated 22.06.2015 opined the sample as misbranded "because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.3 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011 ("the said Regulations" in short) as it gives misleading statement on the label i.e. "No Added MSG". iii) a copy of the Food Analyst Report was sent to the appellant on 23.06.2015 giving him an opportunity to prefer an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act by sending one part of the sample to the Referral Lab, if so desired. But the appellant did not prefer appeal against the Fo Analyst's Report; iv) Thereafter, a complaint was filed against t appellants and others for aforesaid violation before the Ld. ADM. On 29.12.2015, the appellants vide reply while admitting their mistake, submitted that they have informed the manufacturer not to use the FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO said packaging any further for packing the noodles. Sh. Ratan Jeet Singh Gulati vs State Through on 28 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164219645/ 2 3.0 The appellants have challenged the impugned orde inter alia, on the grounds that : i) the Ld. ADM has not properly appreciated t submissions/averments made by the appellants in written statement and treated the same as plea of guilt without applying his mind; ii) Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that the sta printed on the sample "No added MSG" was bona fide and correct and was not to mislead the consumers in any FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO manner; iii) the Ld. ADM did not appreciate either the facts or the law. The appellant/manufacturer had n added MSG and the declaration only to that effect was made on the label. This appeal therefore, Sh. Ratan Jeet Singh Gulati vs State Through on 28 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164219645/ 3 deserves to be dismissed. 6.1 The appellants have challenged the impugned order on various grounds.
texts.arguments: Hence, such a declaration of 'No MSG', without any knowledge/declaration on the appellants' part whether the same is naturally present in the product, could have been deceptive to the consumers. It is pleaded that FSSAI has no power to issue advisories and has placed reliance upon certain judgments in this respect. 6.2 It is also contended by the appellants that the sanction for prosecution was granted without application of mind; and that the Noodles are a proprietary food etc.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Hence, such a declaration of 'No MSG', without any knowledge/declaration on the appellants' part whether the same is naturally present in the product, could have been deceptive to the consumers.
